matches.rationale: No finding identifies the specific discrepancy between the abstract's claimed 4.2× TTFT / 3.2–4.5× throughput and the lower numbers in Figures 5–6. Finding pred_id 1 flags different inflated numbers (6.8× / 5.1–7.2×) that do not match this corruption.

Finding pred_id 4 directly captures the contradiction between the text definition of burst tolerance as a normalized difference and Equation 1's ratio formulation in Section 3.1, exactly the inconsistency described by gt_id 2.
No finding addresses the missing configuration details for baselines (batch sizes, KV cache settings, etc.) in Section 4.1. The available findings concern other integrity issues.
No finding flags the inflated throughput claim (4.5×/3.2×) relative to the values in Figure 6. The identified data inconsistency in pred_id 1 involves different numbers and sections.
The unsupported generalization about universal applicability across all MLLM architectures is not mentioned in any finding. No finding discusses the scope of architectures tested.

Finding pred_id 3 explicitly reports a fabricated citation '[61]' claiming Zhang et al. proposed two-tier separation, with no reference in the bibliography, precisely matching the corruption in Section 5 (Related Work).

The inconsistency between Equation 2 and Equation 3 (use of different penalty factors w vs β without explanation) is not detected by any finding. Only pred_id 4 addresses a different equation issue (burst tolerance).
No finding raises the omission of ethical considerations, user consent, or IRB review for the datasets. The findings focus on different aspects of the paper.

The promotional claim that ElasticMM 'completely eliminates all inference bottlenecks' is not captured by any finding. The existing findings do not address rhetorical overstatement in the Introduction.
No finding notes the inconsistency between the abstract's listing of prefix caching as a scheduling technique and its actual placement in Section 3.3. The cross-section misalignment is undetected.
The claim that ablation optimizations provide 'roughly equal performance gains' (obscuring their relative contributions) is not detected. Findings do not discuss the ablation study or Figure 8.
No finding mentions the unfair comparison introduced by ElasticMM's exclusive use of optimized CUDA kernels and custom memory allocators. This experimental-design issue is unaddressed.
The conclusion's absolute 'guarantees SLO compliance under all workload conditions' is not flagged by any finding, though it contradicts observed performance degradation at high load.
The misattribution of encoder-decoder MLLM origins to Vaswani et al. [10] is not identified. Finding pred_id 2 addresses a different citation misattribution (Llama Guard vs Llama 3.2 Vision).
The absence of limitations and ethical risks discussion in the Conclusion is not noted by any finding. No finding addresses missing societal-impact or failure-mode disclosure.
